interesting_fact: Heaven-Sent Capital Management is a Beijing-based private equity firm founded in August 2006 that focuses on venture capital and buyouts.

name: Evan Williams
current_role: Co-founder and chairman of Mozi (private social app); founder of Medium; co-founder of Obvious Ventures
profile: Nebraska farm kid and college dropout who created Blogger (sold to Google), co-founded Twitter (CEO 2008-2010; on the board until 2019), and founded Medium in 2012 (CEO until 2022). Through Obvious Ventures he backs 'world positive' companies; Beyond Meat was one of its big wins. In late 2024 he co-founded Mozi with CEO Molly DeWolf Swenson, an app built to help friends meet in person.
interesting_fact: He is credited with coining the term 'blogger', and in the mid-1990s he sold tutorial videos that explained the Internet.
deep_cut_fact: Before Pyra and Blogger, he moved to Sebastopol, California in 1996 to work in marketing at O'Reilly Media, later freelancing as a coder (with clients including Intel and HP). While there he started his personal blog, EvHead.com.
notes: His current focus is Mozi, an anti-algorithm social app for meeting in person. For the energy/climate angle, Obvious Ventures' sustainability investing fits. His personal handles (@ev on X and Medium) are widely known, but I did not verify them against a source here.

name: Wang Shusheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, Tianjin DTW Group (大田集团); chairman, Huatian Investment (per older profiles)
profile: Tianjin-born (1954) founder of DTW Group, which he started in 1992 as an air-cargo forwarding and charter business. In 1999 DTW formed a China express joint venture with FedEx. FedEx bought DTW's 50% stake and its domestic network in 2006 for about $400m. He later expanded into logistics (a DTW-Geodis JV), real estate and tourism through Huatian Investment.
interesting_fact: DTW's joint venture with FedEx (1999) gave FedEx its China express network; in early 2006 FedEx bought DTW's 50% of the JV together with its domestic express network.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked at the Tianjin Public Security Bureau. He started DTW in 1992 with 60,000 yuan he had raised himself.
notes: Profile sources are mostly from around 2006. He was off the Hurun lists after 2020, and I found no recent confirmation that he still chairs DTW. The DTW site (dtw.com.cn) returned 403. He has also been a Tianjin CPPCC member. He is low-profile, so a Chinese-language approach via DTW Group is the likeliest route.

name: Hope Welker
current_role: Beneficiary of the Hope Margaret Hancock Trust (stake in Hancock Prospecting); no executive role found
profile: Third child of Gina Rinehart. With her siblings she is a beneficiary of a family trust that holds a large stake in Hancock Prospecting, the Pilbara iron-ore group. She has no public operating role in the business and keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She went to boarding school at Switzerland's Institut Le Rosey.
notes: Very private passive heiress with no operating role in mining, energy or data centres, so a poor fit for the podcast. Most of her press coverage concerns the family trust dispute; avoid it. A search found nothing recent. If approached at all, go through Hancock Prospecting media relations, though they represent the company rather than her.

name: Steve Lansdown
current_role: Owner of Bristol Sport (Bristol City FC, Bristol Bears rugby, Bristol Flyers basketball, Ashton Gate); co-founder of Hargreaves Lansdown
profile: Bristol-born accountant (b. 1952) who co-founded the investment platform Hargreaves Lansdown with Peter Hargreaves in 1981, starting from a bedroom. It grew into the UK's largest retail investment platform. He now lives in Guernsey and has put much of his fortune into Bristol sport through Bristol Sport, which owns Bristol City, Bristol Bears, Bristol Flyers and the Ashton Gate stadium.
interesting_fact: He is one of the longest-serving owners in English professional football, involved with Bristol City for over three decades. In 2025 he sold a majority of Bristol City Women to Mercury13 and kept a minority stake.
deep_cut_fact: He started funding Bristol rugby in the 2008-09 season, when the club looked close to going out of business. After moving to Ashton Gate and rebranding as Bristol Bears, the club won the 2019-20 European Challenge Cup, beating Toulon 32-19. He was made a CBE in 2017 for services to business and the community in Bristol.
notes: Lives in Guernsey. He rarely gives interviews, and his public presence runs through Bristol Sport and its clubs, so the best route is the Bristol Sport / Bristol City media office. I did not verify a specific address. In Aug 2026, Kaizen Gaming CEO George Daskalakis was reported to be in talks to buy a minority stake in Bristol City.

name: Mike Speiser
current_role: Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures; director of Snowflake and Workday
profile: Silicon Valley venture capitalist known for incubating companies in-house at Sutter Hill Ventures, which he joined in 2008 from Yahoo. He helped start Pure Storage, and he co-conceived Snowflake and was its founding CEO (2012-14); Snowflake's 2020 IPO made him a billionaire. He keeps incubating data and infrastructure startups (Sigma Computing, Observe, Clumio, Augment, Reve AI) and investing in companies such as Sila Nano.
interesting_fact: He says he spends about 80% of his time and resources on a single project at a time. By 2021 Sutter Hill had built five companies on top of Snowflake, starting with Lacework.
deep_cut_fact: Before he was a VC he was a founder: he co-founded Bix, a Sutter Hill-backed consumer startup that Yahoo bought in 2006. In 2008 he started assembling Pure Storage with John Colgrove and John Hayes.
notes: Very relevant to data centres: Snowflake, Pure Storage and Sila Nano (battery materials) cover data infrastructure, storage and energy. He gave a long-form interview on the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast (Aug 2025): https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/goldman-sachs-exchanges/finding-the-right-problems-how-sutter-hill-ventures-mike-speiser-creates-great-companies . He keeps a low profile; the best route is via Sutter Hill Ventures, though I did not verify a published contact.

name: Brandt Louie
current_role: Chairman and CEO, H.Y. Louie Co. Ltd. and London Drugs Ltd. (Vancouver)
profile: Fourth-generation head of the Louie family business, founded when his grandfather H.Y. Louie opened a Chinatown store in 1903. Brandt worked as a chartered accountant before joining in 1972 and has led the business since 1998. The Vancouver-based group runs the London Drugs chain and IGA grocery operations and is one of BC's largest private companies. He was SFU's chancellor for six years and was named to the Order of Canada in 2024.
interesting_fact: H.Y. Louie's first store, originally called the Kwong Chong Company, sold seed, fertilizer and wholesale groceries. The family has been in the Vancouver area since the 19th century.
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen fisherman who supports ocean conservation and works with First Nations on preserving fish stocks. In 2023 he spoke in the Senate Chamber in Ottawa about families affected by the 1923 Chinese Exclusion Act, and he was a major catalyst for a national strategy on anti-Asian racism.
notes: Honours include the Order of Canada (2024), the Order of BC and the BC Business Laureates. Former RBC board member. He is approachable through community and civic channels in Vancouver. Older London Drugs press releases list Hartley PR as the media agency, but those contacts date from 2013-15 and may be stale.

name: Mariana Voigt Schwartz Gomes
current_role: Interior designer in Florianópolis; individual shareholder of WEG S.A. (no board or executive role)
profile: Granddaughter of WEG co-founder Werner Ricardo Voigt and one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, Latin America's largest maker of electric motors. WEG is a listed multinational with factories in more than ten countries and about $7bn in annual revenue. She holds no board seat or executive role at WEG and works as an interior designer in Florianópolis, Brazil.
interesting_fact: WEG was founded in 1961 in Jaraguá do Sul by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt with Eggon João da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus. The name WEG is formed from their initials (Werner, Eggon, Geraldo).
notes: Private heir with no public profile; a search found no public design studio page. WEG (motors, transformers, generation and grid equipment) is highly relevant to energy and data centres, but she has no role there. For the WEG angle, go to WEG's investor relations rather than to her.

name: Konstantin Sixt
current_role: Co-CEO (Co-Chairman of the Management Board), Sixt SE
profile: Third-generation member of the Sixt car-rental family. With his brother Alexander he controls about 56% of Sixt SE, and the two have been co-CEOs since June 2021, when their father Erich moved to chair the supervisory board. Konstantin built out Sixt's online business from 2005 and later ran global sales and e-commerce. He has also led marketing, franchise development and the SIXT+ car subscription.
interesting_fact: Sixt was founded in Munich in 1912 by his great-grandfather Martin Sixt. His father Erich took over in 1969, when it had about 200 vehicles, and with his wife Regine built it into a global brand operating in over 100 countries.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing an MSc in International Accounting and Finance at Cass Business School in London, he joined the family firm in 2005 to run its then-small online operations. Ten years later he joined the management board in charge of national and international sales and global e-commerce.
notes: Contact through Sixt corporate communications (press contact Johannes Gunst, per Sixt corporate news releases) or IR. Possible podcast angle: Sixt's EV fleet, charging and digital mobility platform.

name: Chen Jinsong
current_role: Founder of Shenzhen Worldunion Group (世联行, SZ:002285); former chairman, later co-chairman/director (current board status unverified)
profile: Founded Worldunion, the Shenzhen real-estate consultancy and agency that became one of China's largest property-services firms and listed in Shenzhen in 2009. Hurun lists him jointly with Tong Jie. In 2020 his holding vehicle sold about 202m shares to the Zhuhai state-owned Da Hengqin Group. He then stepped down as chairman in favour of Da Hengqin's Hu Jia and became co-chairman.
interesting_fact: In the 2020 deal his holding company World Union China sold a stake to Zhuhai's state-owned Da Hengqin Group, bringing a state-owned shareholder into the private property-services firm he founded. He stayed on as co-chairman.
notes: Known in China as an outspoken property-market commentator. As of 2025-26 Worldunion is chaired by a Da Hengqin executive. His current board status is unclear; check the latest 002285 announcements. Not an energy or data-centre fit.

name: Dan Gertler
current_role: Israeli mining investor (Fleurette Group), active mainly in the Democratic Republic of Congo
profile: Israeli businessman who built a fortune from mining and oil interests in the DRC, starting with diamonds in 1997. In 2017 he sold his stakes in two Congo copper/cobalt mines to Glencore for $960m, netting an estimated $400m. He has been under US sanctions since December 2017 over alleged corrupt deals; Forbes says the sanctions have been eased in recent years.
interesting_fact: His grandfather, Moshe Schnitzer, co-founded the Israel Diamond Exchange in 1947 and was its long-time president.
notes: HIGH-RISK SUBJECT: under US Treasury sanctions (2017, expanded 2018), with ongoing legal and reputational controversy over Congo mining. A spokesman typically declines to comment. He is relevant to cobalt/copper supply chains, but any podcast contact needs legal and editorial review. I did not verify his current sanctions status because the search budget was exhausted.

name: Liu Zhiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Heung Kong Group (香江集团), Guangzhou-based conglomerate
profile: Co-founded Heung Kong Group in 1990 with his wife Zhai Meiqing, who is its president and chairs the listed Shenzhen Heungkong Holding. The Guangzhou-based group grew in real estate and furniture and home-goods retail, then expanded into finance and health care. He has appeared on Hurun's China list continuously since 2004.
interesting_fact: The couple's philanthropy is unusually prominent for a Chinese developer family: his co-founder and wife Zhai Meiqing received the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy in New York in 2017.
notes: His wife Zhai Meiqing is the group's public face and runs its charity work, so she is the more accessible contact. The corporate sites I tried (heungkong.com.cn and others) did not respond, and the search budget ran out before I could find a verified press contact or a sourced deep-cut fact.

name: Bhikhabai Virani
current_role: Co-founder and director, Balaji Wafers Pvt. Ltd. (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: One of the Virani brothers (also spelled Bhikhubhai) who built Balaji Wafers from a wafer stall at Rajkot's Astron Cinema into one of India's largest regional snack makers, dominant in Gujarat and western India. The family has run it with brothers Chandubhai and Kanubhai/Kanjibhai. Selling a minority stake to General Atlantic in January 2026 made them billionaires.
interesting_fact: The business began in 1974 in the canteen of Astron Cinema in Rajkot, and the brand is named after a Balaji temple next to the cinema. Wafers were made at the family home until 1989.
deep_cut_fact: Before snacks, the brothers put the 20,000 rupees their father gave them from selling ancestral farmland into a farm-equipment venture, and it failed. They opened their first wafer factory at Aji GIDC near Rajkot in 1989 and incorporated Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd in 1992.
notes: The email is the company's general contact address published on its homepage, not a dedicated press line. Chandubhai Virani is the public face of the business. The brothers speak mainly Gujarati, so expect a Gujarati-language approach. Spellings vary: Bhikhabhai/Bhikhubhai. Not an energy fit; better as a classic bootstrapped-entrepreneur story.

name: Enrique Cueto
current_role: Former CEO of LATAM Airlines Group (2012-2020); later a board member and member of the Cueto controlling family (current board status unverified)
profile: Chilean business engineer (b. 1959, PUC Chile) whose family built its fortune in aviation. He joined the small cargo carrier Fast Air in 1982, ran LAN Chile from 1994 as it expanded and listed in New York, and co-negotiated the 2010-12 LAN-TAM merger. He then ran the combined LATAM Airlines Group as CEO until 2020.
interesting_fact: He was one of the main negotiators of the 2010-2012 LAN-TAM merger, which created LATAM Airlines Group, Latin America's largest airline group.
deep_cut_fact: His aviation career began in 1982 at Fast Air Carrier, a small Chilean cargo airline founded in 1978, where he became VP of finance within a year. He later served as president of ALTA, the Latin American and Caribbean airline association.
notes: The Spanish Wikipedia article is flagged as outdated (2020), so verify his current LATAM board seat against LATAM's latest governance filings. Possible podcast angle: sustainable aviation fuel and airline energy use. I found no verified personal channels, so go through LATAM corporate communications.
